interactions.summary: Jiang pushes the class toward reading the Bible for themselves, and a student responds with a long question about how intuition, reason, scripture, church authority, and a God beyond all manifestations are supposed to fit together.
Jiang answers by asking what makes scripture hard to read, and the student says the Bible has many versions, which Jiang accepts as part of the problem.

Jiang argues that the Bible cannot be read by logic alone and must be approached through intuition, judgment, faith, scripture, and priestly listening together; the student then restates this through the inside-outside metaphor by proposing that intuition points to a concrete divine reality beyond the self.

claims.claim: A student crystallizes the packet's core contradiction by asking how intuition, rational thought, Bible reading, church forms, and a God beyond all of them can all be necessary at once for approaching the divine.

Jiang says one problem with scripture is textual multiplicity itself: the Bible comes in many versions and is therefore not something that can be naively mastered at the level of simple literal reading.
Jiang argues that the Bible cannot be read adequately through logic alone and instead requires intuition, which becomes the faculty that navigates contradiction and complexity in sacred text.

Jiang compresses Dante's practical path to salvation into a synthesis of church attendance, listening to the priest, reading the Bible, and then exercising one's own judgment, intuition, and faith rather than outsourcing discernment entirely.

The student extends Jiang's inside-outside metaphor by suggesting that if intuition cannot simply absolve the self from everything, then intuition may point beyond the self toward a concrete divine reality.

signature_moments.moment: The student forces the seminar's latent contradiction into the open by asking how to approach a God who exceeds both Bible and church while still being sought through them.
signature_moments.source_phrase: if we presume that god is above all of this
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It converts Jiang's earlier provocation into a serious epistemic problem instead of leaving it at anti-clerical rhetoric.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang laughs off purely logical scripture reading and says the real way through the Bible is intuition.
signature_moments.source_phrase: try reading the bible using logic. good luck with that one
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's sharpest compression of why sacred text requires a non-reductive mode of understanding.

signature_moments.moment: The practical religious path becomes a braid rather than a choice: church, priest, Bible, judgment, intuition, and faith all have to work together.
signature_moments.source_phrase: what he's really saying is, use your own judgment. use your intuition. use your faith
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This keeps Jiang from collapsing into either pure institutional obedience or pure inward subjectivism.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The student's shorthand for why scripture is hard to read directly: textual multiplicity complicates literal certainty and pushes the reader toward interpretation.
Jiang's distilled account of Dantean discernment: external guidance matters, but the person still has to judge inwardly through intuition and faith.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-06-16 packet deepens the prior anti-literalist and anti-monopoly reading by turning it into an epistemology: Jiang now says scripture, priestly guidance, and church practice matter, but only as inputs to intuition, judgment, and faith rather than as substitutes for them.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang says 'what Donnie is saying,' which appears to be an ASR rendering of Dante; the interpretive content is clear even if the name token is noisy.
